[[File:Ryszard Engelking in 2014.jpg|thumb|Engelking in 2014]]
'''Ryszard Engelking''' (16 November 1935 – 16 November 2023) was a Polish mathematician. He was working mainly on [[general topology]]<ref name="Nauki1980">{{cite book|last=Instytut Historii Nauki, Oświaty i Techniki (Polska Akademia Nauki|title=Kwartalnik historii nauki i techniki|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Pw-5AAAAIAAJ|access-date=12 June 2011|year=1980|publisher=Panstwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe.|language=pl|page=704}}</ref> and [[dimension theory]]. He is the author of several influential monographs in this field. The 1989 edition of his ''General Topology'' is nowadays a standard reference for [[topology]].<ref>K.P. Hart, J.-I. Nagata and J.E. Vaughan
Editors, Encyclopedia of general Topology, Elsevier 2003, p. vii</ref> Engelking died on 16 November 2023, his 88th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ryszard Engelking, Warszawa, 20.11.2023 - nekrolog |url=https://nekrologi.wyborcza.pl/0,11,,567891,Ryszard-Engelking-nekrolog.html |access-date=21 November 2023 |website=nekrologi.wyborcza.pl}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Apart from his books, Ryszard Engelking is known, among other things, for a generalization to an arbitrary [[topological space]] of the "Alexandroff double circle",<ref>Haruto Ohta, Special Spaces, Chapter b-13 in Encyclopedia of general Topology.</ref><ref>R. Engelking, On the double circumference of Alexandroff, Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. 16 (1968), 629–634.</ref> for works on [[completely metrizable space]]s, suborderable spaces and [[Order topology|generalized ordered spaces]].<ref>Encyclopedia of general Topology, pp. 204, 206, 252 and 328</ref> The ''Engelking–Karlowicz theorem'', proved together with Monica Karlowicz, is a statement about the existence of a family of functions from <math>2^ \mu</math> to <math>\mu</math> with topological<ref>Ryszard Engelking and Monica Karlowicz, Some theorems of set theory and their topological consequences, [[Fundamenta Mathematicae]], 57, 275–285, 1965.</ref> and [[set theory|set-theoretical]]<ref>
Uri Abraham and [[Menachem Magidor]], Cardinal Arithmetic, Ch. 14 in Handbook of Set Theory ([[Matthew Foreman]], Akihiro Kanamori,
Editors) pp. 1223, 1226.</ref> applications.

== Books ==
Engelking's books include:
*{{cite book | author=R. Engelking | title=Outline of General Topology | publisher= North-Holland, Amsterdam | year=1968 | others=translated from Polish}}
*{{cite book | author=R. Engelking | title=General Topology | publisher=PWN, Warsaw | year=1977 }}
*{{cite book | author=R. Engelking | title=Dimension Theory | publisher= North-Holland, Amsterdam | year=1978 }}
*{{cite book | author=R. Engelking | title=General Topology. Revised and completed edition | publisher=Heldermann Verlag, Berlin | year=1989 | isbn=3-88538-006-4 }}
*{{cite book | author=R. Engelking | title=Theory of Dimensions: Finite and Infinite | publisher=Heldermann Verlag, Berlin | year=1995 | isbn=3-88538-010-2 }}

== Personalia ==
The Polish sociologist [[Barbara Engelking]] is a daughter of Ryszard Engelking.
